claim: In She grabbed me by the arm, the body-part NP and the NP associated with it must be oblique and direct complements of a single verb.
evidence_summary: Chapter 8, p. 681 [9iiia], gives He was wounded in the foot as a contact-with-body-part example. The associated NP is the passive subject.
finding: Extend the condition to a passive subject corresponding to the active object, or state that the condition holds at that level.
proposed_wording: the body-part NP is oblique complement and the associated NP is direct complement (or the corresponding passive subject) of a single verb
inference: Must the associated NP be a direct complement in surface structure?

evidence.passage: §6.1, p. 370. “the body-part NP and the NP with which it is associated are respectively oblique and direct complements of a single verb”.
evidence.example: Page 681 [9iiia] He was wounded in the foot, under “Contact with body-part”.
evidence.establishes: The stated condition excludes the book’s own passive example.
evidence.note: Local source (working note, unpublished draft or local copy); not online.
